name: the-living-atlas
title: The Living Atlas
question: The paper's semantic figures each compile to an executable that runs — but the real test of composition is whether their independently-authored mechanisms share enough interface to COMPOSE. This capstone wires the recurring figure modules (thermal interface, cell↔environment uptake, viability-gated metabolism, the viability monitor, and the division/disintegration rewrites) through shared cell and environment stores and runs them as one whole cell. Do the figures compose into a single cell that grows, divides, and dies?
biological_summary: This is the payoff. Each figure study showed one pattern compiling from draft to executable; here those same mechanisms are wired through shared cell and environment stores into a single running whole cell — and it lives a whole life in one 20-step trajectory. The cell GROWS on the environmental nutrient as viability-gated metabolism converts uptake to biomass (biomass 0.3 → peak ≈5.1). Once biomass crosses the division threshold the rewrite fires ONCE, partitioning it into two daughters (cell_count 1 → 2 at t≈3.4). Then the thermal environment shocks past the tolerance band (temperature 37 → 50 °C at t≈12); the viability monitor reads the interface and collapses viability (1.0 → 0.018), which gates metabolism off and triggers the disintegration rewrite — the maintained boundary fails and biomass decays into molecular debris (debris 0 → 4.87, biomass settling to 0.70). Grow, divide once, die — the paper''s interface→coupling→metabolism→viability→rewrite arc, closed in a single composed cell. Backing this whole-cell payoff is the gallery — all twelve of the paper''s semantic figures, each compiling to an executable that runs to completion (12/12). The same mechanisms that ran as twelve separate figures are the modules wired into this one cell.
claim: The paper's figure mechanisms are modular: wired through shared cell and environment stores they COMPOSE into one whole cell that grows (biomass peak ≈5.1), divides once (cell_count 1 → 2), and dies (viability 1.0 → 0.018 after a thermal shock 37 → 50 °C converts biomass to debris 0 → 4.87). Backing it, all twelve of the paper's semantic figures compile to executables that run to completion (12/12) — the gallery whose modules this cell composes.

findings.statement: The figure modules compose into a cell that GROWS. Confirmed: wired through shared cell and environment stores, viability-gated metabolism turns nutrient uptake into biomass, growing it 0.3 → peak ≈5.1 in one run.
The composed cell DIVIDES ONCE: when biomass crosses the division threshold the rewrite fires a single time, partitioning the cell into two daughters. Confirmed: cell_count 1 → 2 at t≈3.4.

The composed cell DIES. Confirmed: the thermal environment shocks past the tolerance band (temperature 37 → 50 °C at t≈12), the viability monitor collapses viability 1.0 → 0.018, metabolism gates off, and the disintegration rewrite converts biomass to molecular debris 0 → 4.87.

The whole-cell payoff rests on a gallery of running parts: all twelve of the paper's semantic figures compile to executables that run to completion. Confirmed: 12/12, one witness being fig07's F1Fo ATP synthase charging its port 0 → 100.

regression_compatibility.basis: The composed whole-cell composite runs 20 steps to completion and all twelve figure executables run to completion (12/12) via scripts/render_study_evidence.py.

biological_validation.basis: The composed cell reproduces a full life arc from its modular parts — it grows (biomass 0.3 → peak ≈5.1), divides once (cell_count 1 → 2), and dies (viability 1.0 → 0.018 after temperature 37 → 50 °C; debris 0 → 4.87) — so the paper's interface→coupling→metabolism→viability→rewrite arc is mechanism-driven, produced by wiring independently-authored figure modules through shared stores.

explanatory_gain.basis: Composing the figures' recurring modules into one cell that grows, divides once, and dies turns "the figures compose" from a claim into a single measured trajectory — backed by a gallery of all twelve figures each running on its own.

conclusion:
## Claims
- The paper's figure mechanisms are modular: wired through shared cell and environment stores they compose into one whole cell that grows, divides once, and dies. The same modules also each run as twelve standalone figure executables (12/12).

## Evidence
- **GROWS** — viability-gated metabolism grows biomass 0.3 → peak ≈5.1 on the depleting nutrient
- **DIVIDES-ONCE** — the division rewrite fires once: cell_count 1 → 2, two daughters, at t≈3.4
- **DIES** — thermal shock (temperature 37 → 50 °C at t≈12) collapses viability 1.0 → 0.018; disintegration converts biomass to debris 0 → 4.87
- **TWELVE-RUN** — all 12 fig*-executable composites compile and run to completion (12/12); fig07's ATP synthase charging 0 → 100 witnesses the gallery

## Limitations
- Toy-real composition: the whole cell wires illustrative figure modules through shared stores; it is a demonstration that the mechanisms COMPOSE into one grow→divide→die trajectory, not a calibrated whole-cell model. One deterministic run.

## Next steps
- Run the composed whole cell across replicate seeds and thermal schedules; grow the composition beyond the current module set toward a calibrated cell.
